natural_body: Targeted 40% discounts boost acquisition but sharply damage retention.

first.rationale: The two symptoms that are actually degrading (onboarding completion -4% QoQ, activation -6% QoQ) point at the funnel stage covered by memory_86 (shortened onboarding lifts completion and time-to-value) and memory_31 (fewer required signup fields lifts first-week activation). Those are the two I want the archive to return, because they are the memories doing the most load-bearing work for the decision and both are old (day 12 and day 52) relative to a funnel that has since shifted; I want to see original effect sizes, segment definitions, and whether the lift was measured on activation alone or carried through to retained revenue. I am deliberately not spending budget on memory_73: the competitor's entry pricing makes promotional_pricing the tempting reflex, but memory_73 already says 40% discounts sharply damage retention, and the objective is sustainable long-term qualified revenue, so matching price would buy acquisition against the stated goal even if the memory is somewhat stale. Verifying it could only tempt me into a direction I have independent reason to avoid. memory_57 (referrals) and memory_91 (activation messaging) are plausible but address healthy or secondary surfaces; memory_44 (enterprise sales-assist) addresses a segment that is not the one under pressure. The main downstream risk I am flagging: memory_31's mechanism is cutting required signup fields, and those fields are plausibly what routes enterprise prospects into the demo-request path that memory_44 says produces better pipeline quality. A naive field cut could lift SMB activation while quietly degrading enterprise qualification, which is exactly the kind of trade that looks like a win on the experiment metric and a loss on qualified revenue. So the test must instrument enterprise routing and downstream pipeline quality, not just activation and completion. I am running this at standard experiment scale rather than broad rollout: the directional evidence is consistent across two independent memories, but neither is confirmed to track revenue rather than activation, and both predate the current competitive environment. If the archive shows either memory measured only proximate activation, or shows the signup-field cut removed qualification data, I will narrow to a guarded test that preserves qualification fields and shortens only post-signup onboarding steps.
